newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME base metal complex seen quiet before holidays.
newsitem.headline: LME base metal complex seen quiet before holidays.

text.p: The London Metal exchange (LME) base metal complex will probably drift sideways later on Friday with little in the way of leads seen moving the market ahead of the long weekend, traders said.
"I think it will be pretty dull this afternoon," a dealer for a European metal trading company said. "Quite a few people are already out for the holidays."
The LME will be closed on Monday for a holiday.
LME metal brokers Brandeis said in its daily review that copper "looks to be settling into a US$2,320/390 trading range with a slight bias to the upside".
Macquarie said in its daily report the May Day holiday celebrated in most of Europe kept interest in the complex "depleted and hence volumes remained light".
Three month copper was quoted by the trade at 0200 GMT at around $2,361/66 a tonne after being indicated on Thursday at $2,364/67 a tonne.

"Copper may drift lower this afternoon," the general manager of a Japanese metal trading firm said. "But the market will not be active because of the holidays coming up and the Golden Week holiday season in Japan."
Far East dealers said they were keeping an eye on the rash of strikes which have hit copper mines in Chile, the world's largest producer of the red metal.
A strike began on Wednesday at the Quebrada Blanca mine while another strike by some 350 of the 2,000 workers at the Escondida mine in northern Chile is still unresolved.
"The trade is talking about the strikes although there has been no impact so far," a trader said.
Regional business was subdued except for aluminium demand which was said to remain firm because of strong offtake from buyers in Japan and Southeast Asia.
Three month aluminium was quoted by the trade at around 0200 GMT at $1,627/31 a tonne against the close in London on Thursday at $1,628.
Copper and aluminium inventories were expected to dip when the LME stocks report is released at 0800 GMT.
